title: Brand as Memory: VLMs Trust the Masthead, Not the Evidence
hook: Show a VLM the same article under a trusted outlet's logo versus an unknown one, and its verdict swings by 1.8x — a bias localized to three specific layers and steerable away.
key_points: VLMs increasingly read news as images, where publisher identity (masthead, logo, domain) is visually present alongside the content.
CueTrust benchmark: across 7 VLMs and 5 surface cues, only outlet identity moves credibility judgments — not a named author, in-text authority, or page layout (clean negative controls).
Swapping only the masthead shifts credibility across an ~11 log-odds range that correlates with real-world outlet ratings (rho = 0.88 vs. Media Bias/Fact Check).
The bias is causally formed at layers 19-21, carried by interpretable sparse-autoencoder features, and overrides content evidence by about 1.8x.
Steering the localized direction cuts the override by 41% and generalizes to outlets never seen during steering.
content_html: Feed a vision-language model the same article image twice, changing only the masthead logo at the top, and its judgment of how credible the content is can swing dramatically — even though nothing in the actual text changed.
extra_html: As VLMs increasingly read news and web pages as images rather than plain text, the publisher's identity is visually baked into the input alongside the content. The authors introduce CueTrust, a cross-model diagnostic testing which surface cues override an article's content evidence across seven VLMs and five candidate cues. Only outlet identity moves the needle — firing consistently from the masthead name, the logo image, or the bare domain — while clean negative controls (a named author, in-text authority claims, page layout) don't. For the masthead specifically, the effect is large and mechanistically traceable: swapping only the logo moves credibility across roughly an 11 log-odds range that tracks real professional outlet ratings (rho = 0.88 against Media Bias/Fact Check), is causally formed at layers 19-21, and is carried by interpretable sparse-autoencoder features that recur at the same relative location in a second model family. The prior overrides actual content by about 1.8x. Encouragingly, steering the localized direction cuts that override by 41% and generalizes to outlets the steering never saw — evidence the bias is causally used, not just decodable, and that it can be dialed back. Chih-Ting Liao and Xin Cao, arXiv 2026.

related.title: When Flattery Breaks the Model: Sycophancy as a Driver of Emergent Misalignment
related.hook: Teaching a model to flatter users into agreeing with wrong opinions can trigger broad misalignment — and learnable 'gates' can find and suppress the unsafe directions to reverse it.

related.title: SAE Interventions Are Unreliable
related.hook: Clamping a 'harmful' sparse-autoencoder feature looks like it stops bad behavior — but this paper recovers it 95.8% of the time, exposing the gap between feature-level and real control.

related.title: Scaling Monosemanticity: Features from Claude 3 Sonnet
related.hook: Does dictionary learning survive at production scale? Anthropic found millions of features in Claude 3 Sonnet — and could steer the model by turning one up.

flashcards.prompt: What is the 'Source-Override Index' in the CueTrust benchmark measuring?
flashcards.back_html: How much a surface source cue (like a masthead, logo, or domain) shifts a VLM's credibility judgment relative to the article's actual content evidence.

flashcards.prompt: Which surface cues actually moved VLM credibility judgments in the study?

choices.text: Outlet identity — masthead name, logo image, or bare domain

flashcards.explanation_html: The clean negative controls (author, in-text authority, layout) didn't move judgments; only outlet-identity cues did, and they worked whether shown as text, logo, or domain.

flashcards.prompt: Where is the brand-credibility bias causally located, and what happens when you steer against it?
flashcards.back_html: It's causally formed at layers 19-21, carried by interpretable sparse-autoencoder features. Steering the localized direction reduces the content-override effect by 41%, and this generalizes to outlets not used during steering.

flashcards.prompt: How closely did the masthead-swap credibility shift track real-world media bias ratings?

choices.text: Strongly — rho = 0.88 against Media Bias/Fact Check ratings
Not at all — the two measures were uncorrelated
Only for one specific VLM out of seven tested

flashcards.explanation_html: The ~11 log-odds credibility range from swapping only the masthead correlated at rho = 0.88 with independent professional outlet ratings, suggesting the model has internalized real-world outlet reputations.
